title: Restricted localStorage can lose failed-logout fail-closed state across Dashboard reload
classification: session/logout recovery correctness; not an authentication bypass exploit
preconditions: The logout request does not complete server revocation/cookie clearing, for example because the network request fails before reaching the server.
The browser retains the still-valid HttpOnly refresh cookie.
localStorage writes and reads are unavailable/throw across the subsequent page reload, while cookies remain usable.
The page is reloaded before an explicit successful logout retry or explicit credential login.

source_to_sink.evidence: logout() calls markLogoutUnconfirmed(), clears the in-memory identity boundary, then dispatches POST logout. markLogoutUnconfirmed always sets the current instance boolean true but swallows localStorage.setItem failure. A fresh client starts with logoutUnconfirmed=false; hasUnconfirmedLogout catches localStorage.getItem failure and returns false.
On a fresh provider with no in-memory session, hasUnconfirmedLogout=true blocks bootstrap refresh, but false enters the automatic client.refresh() branch. Thus the lost marker is the bootstrap gate.

Login issues a Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict refresh cookie scoped to /v1/staff/auth. Refresh authenticates from that cookie and rotates it. Cookie clearing occurs on definitive refresh authentication failure or successful logout response handling; a client-side network failure before logout reaches/completes the server does not independently clear the browser cookie.
Server session revocation occurs only when logoutStaffSession executes with a valid refresh credential. There is no independent client-side revocation mechanism.

impact: The current runtime is fail-closed immediately after logout is pressed, but under the stated restricted-storage/network conditions a reload can forget that logout is unconfirmed and automatically refresh the still-live server session. This violates the Dashboard's stated fail-closed logout continuity guarantee and may restore protected access on the same browser after the user attempted to sign out.
counterevidence_and_bounds: This does not bypass server authentication: automatic refresh still requires a valid refresh cookie and server-valid session.
If logout reaches the server and revokes the session, subsequent refresh is denied and the server clears the refresh cookie.
If cookies are unavailable whenever localStorage is unavailable in a given browser mode, the vulnerable precondition is absent because refresh cannot succeed.
Within the same JavaScript runtime, the in-memory logoutUnconfirmed boolean remains true even when localStorage persistence fails, so the gap is specifically cross-reload/new-client continuity.

A successful explicit credential login calls clearLogoutUnconfirmed after the server accepts credentials; treating this as an intentional explicit re-authentication is coherent and is not the problematic automatic-refresh path.

existing_test_cross_check.evidence: The existing failed-logout/reload test proves the desired fail-closed behavior when localStorage works: the marker is persisted and a new client reads it. Its storage spies do not throw, so it does not cover the restricted-storage branch. Repository search found no failed-logout test that denies localStorage across a fresh client/provider bootstrap.

missing_controlled_evidence: No unit/browser reproduction was executed in C003 because this transfer explicitly forbids tests. Controlled confirmation should simulate localStorage set/get throwing, a failed logout request, a fresh StaffAuthClient/StaffAuthProvider, and a surviving refresh cookie/refresh success, then prove bootstrap does not auto-restore after remediation.
remediation_options: Fail closed on storage-read unavailability during bootstrap instead of treating it as no pending logout. This is simple but intentionally disables automatic cookie-based session restoration for storage-denied browsers until explicit login.

Alternatively persist a deny-only logout-pending marker in another verified durable browser mechanism that remains available when refresh cookies are available, then require successful server logout or explicit credential login to clear it.
Whichever design is chosen, add a regression test for failed logout + storage denial + reload/new client and keep the existing successful-storage continuity tests.
regression_risks: Changing storage read failure to fail-closed can reduce convenience by forcing explicit login after every reload for browsers that block localStorage but permit cookies.
A second persistence channel must be deny-only, scoped narrowly and must not contain access/refresh credentials or become an authority source.
Marker clearing on explicit successful login must remain intentional so a user can recover from an unconfirmable prior logout without a permanent lockout.
Do not weaken identity/session generation fencing or replay a rejected logout/mutation implicitly while fixing bootstrap behavior.
duplicate_status: No existing Dashboard finding covering failed-logout restricted-storage continuity was found in the frozen audit register. Related only by failure class to CUST-001/#356 (restricted preference storage), but impact and code path are distinct. No GitHub issue was created by worker-7.
